question: Which population group is most appropriately targeted for a quarantine protocol?

options.A: Patients with laboratory-confirmed disease diagnoses
options.B: Community members requesting routine preventative vaccinations
options.C: Healthy people with a history of contact with a contagious case
options.D: Healthcare workers on routine hospital shifts

explanation: Because quarantined individuals do not currently show symptoms, they consist of healthy contacts who need observation during the incubation period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h1)

question: How does isolation differ fundamentally from quarantine?

options.A: Isolation requires voluntary compliance rather than legal enforcement
options.B: Isolation applies exclusively to individuals with confirmed contagious illnesses
options.C: Isolation is utilized only for chronic non-communicable disorders
options.D: Isolation restricts healthy people who traveled abroad recently

explanation: Isolation separates sick, infectious people from healthy people, whereas quarantine separates potentially exposed, healthy people. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient testing positive for Lassa fever is moved to a private ward away from other patients. What public health strategy is being implemented?

options.A: Contact tracing
options.B: Active quarantine
options.C: Medical isolation
options.D: Community sanitization

explanation: Since the patient has a confirmed diagnosis and active illness, separating them from others constitutes isolation rather than quarantine. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h2)

question: What primary piece of legislation grants the Nigerian government authority to declare public health quarantines?

options.A: The National Health Insurance Scheme Act
options.B: The Quarantine Act
options.C: The Nursing and Midwifery Decree
options.D: The Essential Drugs Policy

explanation: The Quarantine Act provides the legal basis in Nigeria for executing emergency measures to prevent the introduction and spread of dangerous infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why must authorities provide basic necessities like food and water to individuals placed under mandatory quarantine?

options.A: To prevent legal challenges under international trade agreements
options.B: To maintain ethical standards and protect human rights during confinement
options.C: To ensure compliance through financial penalties if supplies are wasted
options.D: To reduce the operational budget of the local government council

explanation: Restricting personal liberty ethically obligates the state to provide basic human needs such as nutrition, water, shelter, and medical support. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h3)

question: When is home quarantine most appropriate for an exposed individual?

options.A: When the individual refuses institutional medical oversight entirely
options.B: When the household can support separation and adequate sanitation
options.C: When the household lacks running water and electricity
options.D: When the individual develops severe respiratory distress

explanation: Home quarantine works safely only if the physical environment allows the exposed person to remain separated from other household members. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h4)

question: A traveller arrives at Murtala Muhammed International Airport from an epicentre of a novel viral outbreak and has no permanent residence in the city. What type of quarantine setting is most suitable?

options.A: Unrestricted self-monitoring within local markets
options.B: Immediate hospital intensive care admission
options.C: Facility-based or institutional quarantine
options.D: Home quarantine with daily phone check-ins

explanation: Without a permanent home or local support system, the traveller must be placed in a designated institutional quarantine facility managed by health authorities. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which practice is most essential for preventing cross-contamination inside a quarantine facility?

options.A: Frequent hand hygiene and proper surface disinfection
options.B: Eliminating all personal belongings brought by residents
options.C: Restricting natural ventilation in all residential rooms
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to all residents daily

explanation: Hand hygiene and cleaning environmental surfaces are foundational pillars of stopping pathogen spread in any group setting. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: What should a nurse advise a resident in home quarantine regarding everyday household items?

options.A: Soak all shared bedding in bleach solution for forty-eight hours continuously
options.B: Avoid sharing personal items like towels, cups, and utensils
options.C: Dispose of all clothing items after wearing them once
options.D: Share eating utensils after washing them with cold water only

explanation: To prevent indirect contact transmission, quarantined individuals must avoid sharing personal utensils, cups, towels, and bedding with others. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the standard clinical assessment performed routinely on individuals in quarantine?

options.A: Performing daily diagnostic blood cultures and biopsies
options.B: Administering complete neurological reflex examinations
options.C: Measuring body temperature and screening for specific symptoms
options.D: Suturing minor lacerations and changing surgical dressings

explanation: Routine temperature checks and symptom screening help detect the earliest signs of active disease during the incubation period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h6)

question: During a morning health check in a quarantine facility, a resident reports sudden onset fever and headache. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Discharge the resident immediately to relieve facility overcrowding
options.B: Advise the resident to sleep and re-check their temperature next week
options.C: Initiate protocol to transfer the resident to an isolation facility
options.D: Prescribe heavy doses of prophylactic antimalarials without testing

explanation: The appearance of symptoms means the individual is no longer a candidate for quarantine and must be moved to isolation for medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which psychological response is most commonly observed among individuals undergoing mandatory quarantine?

options.A: Euphoria and extreme relaxation
options.B: Enhanced cognitive performance and focus
options.C: Anxiety, frustration, and emotional distress
options.D: Complete indifference to surroundings

explanation: Sudden confinement, fear of illness, and separation from loved ones frequently induce psychological distress and anxiety in quarantined persons. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: How can a nurse best help alleviate the emotional burden of a resident experiencing distress in quarantine?

options.A: Provide clear timelines, empathetic listening, and connection channels
options.B: Limit their access to information to prevent any confusion
options.C: Isolate them completely from staff interaction to maintain quiet
options.D: Inform them that complaining will extend their mandatory stay

explanation: Transparent communication, empathetic support, and maintaining contact with loved ones via technology significantly reduce psychological distress. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is the involvement of local and religious leaders crucial during a community quarantine effort?

options.A: They help build trust and communicate accurate messages effectively
options.B: They are trained to conduct clinical diagnostic lab tests
options.C: They possess the legal authority to arrest non-compliant residents
options.D: They supply the financial budget for institutional feeding programs

explanation: Trusted community and religious leaders hold significant influence in local populations, helping dispel myths and encourage cooperation with health directives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary consequence of widespread misinformation regarding a quarantine directive in a local neighbourhood?

options.A: Increased compliance with daily health surveillance checks
options.B: Panic, hostility, and concealment of potential illness symptoms
options.C: Improved funding and resource allocation from donors
options.D: Faster eradication of the infectious disease agent

explanation: When rumors and misinformation spread, people become fearful and distrustful, often hiding symptoms and avoiding public health authorities. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which of the following is a core responsibility of the community health nurse in quarantine management?

options.A: Manufacturing personal protective equipment for hospitals
options.B: Managing international travel flight schedules and visas
options.C: Drafting national legislation for epidemic disease control
options.D: Conducting daily health monitoring and providing health education

explanation: Community health nurses directly execute symptom surveillance, offer guidance, and educate residents and families throughout the quarantine period. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: What makes the community health nurse uniquely positioned for successful quarantine oversight in local settings?

options.A: Their exclusive focus on high-technology surgical interventions
options.B: Their authority to impose financial fines on community members
options.C: Their ability to practice independently without any guidelines
options.D: Their deep familiarity with local culture, language, and family structures

explanation: Community health nurses understand local cultural nuances and build rapport easily, which fosters better cooperation and trust during health crises. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: What defines a non-human reservoir in the context of public health?

options.A: An organism or environment where a pathogen naturally lives and multiplies
options.B: Any inanimate medical equipment contaminated with biological fluids
options.C: A pharmaceutical substance used to neutralize pathogenic bacteria
options.D: The primary human host who transmits an infection during an outbreak

explanation: Reservoirs serve as the natural habitat where infectious agents survive, reproduce, and rely upon for their primary existence. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why can certain pathogens persist indefinitely in non-human reservoirs without causing symptoms in those hosts?

options.A: Environmental temperature prevents the pathogen from releasing toxins
options.B: Non-human hosts possess artificial immunity acquired through routine vaccination
options.C: The pathogen has evolved a commensal or tolerant relationship with the host species
options.D: Pathogens only produce disease molecules when exposed to human blood

explanation: Long-term co-evolution between pathogens and specific non-human hosts often establishes biological balance, preventing severe disease in the reservoir itself. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which animal serves as the primary natural reservoir for the Lassa virus in West Africa?

options.A: Free-roaming cattle
options.B: Domestic canines
options.C: Freshwater snails
options.D: Mastormys rodents

explanation: Multimammate rats of the Mastomys genus shed Lassa virus through their excreta, driving regional transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h2)

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian settlement is planning education on rabies prevention. Which animal population should be the primary focus of this campaign?

options.A: Bovine livestock
options.B: Swine populations
options.C: Domestic dogs
options.D: Freshwater rodents

explanation: Dogs account for the vast majority of human rabies cases globally, making canine vaccination and bite management central to control strategies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of reservoir destruction in communicable disease control?

options.A: To manufacture synthetic antibodies for clinical treatment
options.B: To provide temporary symptomatic relief to infected human patients
options.C: To eliminate the natural source and habitat where a pathogen multiplies
options.D: To alter human genetic susceptibility against viral pathogens

explanation: Destroying or modifying the reservoir removes the foundational breeding ground that sustains the infectious agent in nature. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which intervention represents an environmental modification method of controlling a rodent reservoir?

options.A: Clearing tall grass and debris away from building foundations
options.B: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to domestic cattle herds
options.C: Isolating human patients in negative-pressure hospital wards
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets to pregnant women

explanation: Environmental modification involves altering physical surroundings to deny pests and vectors shelter and food sources. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which sanitation practice directly helps reduce synanthropic rodent populations around human dwellings?

options.A: Boiling drinking water vigorously for ten minutes
options.B: Washing bed linens in hot water weekly
options.C: Using alcohol-based hand sanitizers before meals
options.D: Storing food in tightly sealed, chew-proof containers

explanation: Denying access to food sources is a cornerstone of environmental sanitation designed to discourage rodent infestation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h4)

question: How do vector control strategies interrupt the cycle of zoonotic or vector-borne diseases?

options.A: By altering the genetic structure of the pathogen inside the human body
options.B: By converting wild animal reservoirs into domesticated pets
options.C: By boosting human antibody titers against opportunistic fungal infections
options.D: By breaking the chain of transmission between the reservoir and the human host

explanation: Vector control targets the intermediary organisms that transport pathogens from infected reservoirs to susceptible people. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of mass animal vaccination programs in public health?

options.A: To cure animals already suffering from chronic bacterial sepsis
options.B: To establish herd immunity and prevent zoonotic spillover to humans
options.C: To replace environmental sanitation measures entirely
options.D: To accelerate the growth rate of livestock for commercial markets

explanation: Immunizing domestic animals stops infections at the source, drastically reducing the likelihood of transmission to human handlers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h5)

question: What does the One Health framework emphasize in disease eradication efforts?

options.A: The isolation of veterinary medicine from mainstream clinical nursing
options.B: The complete reliance on human pharmaceutical interventions during epidemics
options.C: The elimination of all wild animal species to ensure total safety
options.D: The interconnection between human health, animal health, and the shared environment

explanation: One Health recognizes that human, animal, and environmental health are deeply linked and require collaborative, multidisciplinary interventions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which factor most commonly causes community resistance to animal culling or reservoir control policies?

options.A: Strict enforcement of water purification guidelines by local councils

options.C: Excessive availability of free veterinary medicines in local clinics
options.D: Lack of cultural consultation and economic compensation for livestock owners

explanation: When communities lose livestock without dialogue or financial recourse, compliance with disease control initiatives drops sharply. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why is participatory community engagement essential when implementing environmental sanitation programs?

options.A: It fosters local ownership and ensures long-term behavioral sustainability
options.B: It replaces the need for government-funded healthcare infrastructure
options.C: It prevents infectious agents from mutating in laboratory settings
options.D: It legally binds citizens to pay municipal sanitation taxes monthly

explanation: Involving community members directly in planning and execution builds lasting habits that outlast short-term public health campaigns. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing intervention in the control of reservoir-borne diseases?

options.A: Performing surgical culling of wild animal populations
options.B: Providing health education on safe food preparation
options.C: Advocating for community-based sanitation resources
options.D: Conducting contact tracing and surveillance monitoring

explanation: Culling wild animals is typically managed by veterinary and wildlife authorities, whereas nurses focus on human health, education, and clinical care. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why does nomadic pastoralism present a unique challenge for controlling zoonotic diseases in parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Constant migration across borders complicates livestock tracking and vaccination coverage
options.B: Traditional housing structures lack adequate ventilation for disease containment
options.C: Nomadic populations refuse to interact with any form of modern medical personnel

explanation: Frequent movement makes it difficult for public health teams to administer scheduled vaccinations or monitor disease outbreaks in herds. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the term for the habitat where an infectious agent normally lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Infectious vector
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: A reservoir serves as the natural habitat and source for a pathogen, allowing it to survive and multiply before infecting a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is understanding the chain of infection vital for community health nursing?

options.A: It helps predict the exact genetic mutation rate of viral pathogens.
options.B: It determines the financial cost of manufactured pharmaceutical vaccines.
options.C: It allows nurses to target interventions and break the cycle of disease spread.
options.D: It eliminates the need for personal protective equipment in hospital wards.

explanation: Every link in the infection chain represents a vulnerable point where targeted public health measures can stop an outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Quarantine uses chemical disinfectants, while isolation relies entirely on surgical masks.
options.B: Isolation separates infected people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy individuals.
options.C: Isolation is voluntary, but quarantine is legally mandated by federal law.
options.D: Isolation applies only to animals, whereas quarantine is strictly for human patients.

explanation: Isolation is used for those already sick with a contagious illness, whereas quarantine is reserved for those who were exposed but are not yet symptomatic. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient diagnosed with active lassa fever is placed in a designated negative-pressure room. Which source-control strategy does this represent?

options.A: Chemoprophylaxis
options.B: Quarantine
options.C: Herd immunity
options.D: Isolation

explanation: Placing a confirmed case in a restricted environment to prevent spreading the pathogen to others is the definition of isolation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which personal protective equipment is specifically required when caring for a patient with an airborne infection like tuberculosis?

options.A: Impermeable plastic apron
options.B: N95 respirator
options.C: Standard surgical mask
options.D: Disposable latex gloves

explanation: Airborne pathogens travel on tiny droplet nuclei that penetrate standard surgical masks, requiring tightly fitted particulate respirators like the N95. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why are droplet precautions effective over only short distances, typically within one meter of the patient?

options.A: Room temperature air currents immediately dissolve the moisture surrounding the pathogen.
options.B: Human skin absorbs the moisture droplets before they can travel across open spaces.
options.C: Hospital ventilation systems create a vacuum that sucks droplets toward the ceiling.
options.D: The particles are heavy enough that gravity quickly pulls them down to the ground.

explanation: Droplets are relatively large and heavy compared to airborne nuclei, meaning they settle rapidly out of the air within a short radius. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is a vehicle in the context of disease transmission?

options.A: A living insect that transmits parasites through its salivary glands
options.B: A domestic animal that serves as the primary biological reservoir for a virus
options.C: A non-living intermediary like water, food, or air that carries a pathogen
options.D: An ambulance used to transport infectious patients to regional treatment centers

explanation: Vehicles are inanimate objects or substances, such as contaminated water or food supplies, that deliver infectious agents to a host. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h4)

question: A community health nurse distributes insecticide-treated nets and teaches residents to clear stagnant puddles around their homes. Which transmission pathway is being targeted?

options.A: Airborne transmission
options.B: Vehicle-borne transmission
options.C: Direct contact transmission
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Mosquitoes act as vectors for diseases like malaria, so controlling their populations and preventing bites interrupts vector-borne spread. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h4)

question: What type of immunity is conferred when a patient receives pre-formed immunoglobulins after an accidental needlestick injury?

options.A: Herd immunity
options.B: Innate immunity
options.C: Active immunity
options.D: Passive immunity

explanation: Passive immunity involves introducing ready-made antibodies into a host to provide immediate, short-term protection without engaging their own immune system. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h5)

question: How does achieving high community vaccination coverage protect unvaccinated individuals?

options.A: It forces all local pathogens to undergo spontaneous genetic mutation into harmless forms.
options.B: It reduces the overall number of susceptible hosts, making it difficult for the pathogen to circulate.
options.C: It creates an impenetrable physical fence around the entire residential district.
options.D: It chemically alters the surrounding air to destroy floating viral particles.

explanation: Herd immunity occurs when a large percentage of the population is immune, drastically lowering the chance that an infected person will encounter someone susceptible. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is an essential community surveillance duty performed by nurses during potential disease outbreaks?

options.A: Reporting cases of communicable diseases to public health authorities
options.B: Manufacturing synthetic vaccines in local clinic laboratories
options.C: Enforcing mandatory imprisonment for non-compliant citizens
options.D: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics without diagnostic testing

explanation: Timely reporting of infectious diseases allows public health agencies to track outbreaks and deploy coordinated intervention strategies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why must community health nurses adapt their health education messages to fit local cultural practices?

options.A: Traditional herbal remedies always neutralize synthetic pharmaceutical interventions.
options.B: Cultural alignment ensures that the community understands, accepts, and adopts the preventive behaviors.
options.C: Standard medical terminology is illegal to use outside of tertiary hospital settings.
options.D: Local governments fine clinics that fail to use traditional folklore stories in lectures.

explanation: Health education is only effective if the target audience relates to the message and trusts the messenger, making cultural competence critical for behavioral change. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between original Universal Precautions and modern Standard Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions apply only to surgical wards
options.B: Universal Precautions apply exclusively to airborne pathogens
options.C: Universal Precautions require the mandatory use of respirators for all patients
options.D: Standard Precautions include all body fluids and moist secretions

explanation: While original Universal Precautions focused specifically on blood and blood-contaminated fluids, Standard Precautions expanded coverage to include all body fluids, non-intact skin, and mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do healthcare professionals treat all patients as potentially infectious under Standard Precautions?

options.A: Laboratory diagnostic tests are too expensive for routine use
options.B: Patients prefer knowing that strict barriers are being utilized
options.C: Infected individuals can be asymptomatic and unaware of their status
options.D: Hospital management mandates this to conserve cleaning supplies

explanation: Many patients carrying bloodborne or other pathogens show no outward symptoms, making universal barrier use essential to prevent silent transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: A nurse working in a rural clinic experiences a temporary interruption in running water. What is the most appropriate immediate action for hand hygiene compliance?

options.A: Perform hand hygiene using dry tissue paper instead of washing
options.B: Postpone all nursing procedures until municipal water supply is restored
options.C: Use alcohol-based hand rub or stored clean water with soap via alternative dispensers
options.D: Proceed with patient care while wearing sterile gloves without washing hands

explanation: When running water fails, alternative dispensing methods like stored water systems or alcohol-based hand rubs ensure hand hygiene protocols are maintained. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is NOT an acceptable response to resource shortages regarding Personal Protective Equipment?

options.A: Using alternative dispensing methods for handwashing water
options.B: Procuring emergency stocks through hospital administrative channels
options.C: Reusing single-use disposable gloves between multiple different patients
options.D: Prioritizing PPE usage for high-risk invasive procedures

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items; reusing them across different patients crosses contamination barriers and spreads pathogens rapidly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for removing gloves first during the PPE doffing sequence?

options.A: Gloves typically carry the highest microbial and fluid contamination load
options.B: Removing gloves allows the nurse to breathe more comfortably
options.C: Gloves are the cheapest items of protective equipment
options.D: Gowns cannot be unfastened while wearing tight gloves

explanation: Because gloves touch patients and contaminated surfaces directly, removing them first prevents accidental transfer of pathogens to other parts of the body or clothing during doffing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to assist a physician with an incision and drainage of a deep, abscessed wound that is expected to spray purulent material. Which combination of PPE is most appropriate?

options.A: Surgical mask, clean gloves, and a hair net
options.B: N95 respirator and sterile gloves only
options.C: Gown, surgical mask, eye protection, and gloves
options.D: Sterile gloves and an apron only

explanation: Procedures likely to generate splashes of body fluids require full barrier protection including a gown, mask, eye protection, and gloves to protect skin, mucous membranes, and clothing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly preferred over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: At the beginning and end of an eight-hour nursing shift
options.B: Whenever working in a busy emergency department
options.C: Immediately before administering oral medications
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material or blood

explanation: Organic matter and blood physical impede alcohol-based rubs; physical washing with soap and water is required to remove visible soil. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the second moment for hand hygiene?

options.A: Before clean or aseptic procedures
options.B: Before touching a patient
options.C: After body fluid exposure risk
options.D: After touching patient surroundings

explanation: The second moment requires hand hygiene immediately before performing clean or aseptic tasks to prevent introducing pathogens into vulnerable patient sites. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the recommended safe method for handling a used hypodermic needle if recapping is unavoidable?

options.A: Bend the needle with forceps before placing it on a tray
options.B: Pass the unsheathed needle to a colleague for disposal
options.C: Use a one-handed scoop technique to guide the needle into the cap
options.D: Hold the cap with the opposite hand and push the needle firmly inward

question: At what fill level should a designated sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: When it reaches the three-quarters full line
options.B: When it is completely full to the brim
options.C: Whenever the container starts to feel heavy
options.D: At the end of every weekly ward shift

explanation: Sharps containers should never be overfilled; sealing them at the three-quarters mark prevents accidental punctures from protruding needles. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: How should a nurse manage a fresh, large puddle of spilled blood on a clinic floor?

options.A: Pour hot water over the spill and leave it to evaporate naturally
options.B: Call the maintenance department and leave the room unlocked until they arrive
options.C: Sweep the blood away immediately using a dry broom and dustpan
options.D: Cover the spill with absorbent material, apply a chlorine-based disinfectant, and wipe after contact time

explanation: Blood spills must be absorbed first, then disinfected with an appropriate chlorine solution like sodium hypochlorite to inactive bloodborne viruses safely. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which waste stream is typically designated for general, non-hazardous administrative rubbish and food waste in a hospital?

options.A: Black bins
options.B: Brown chemical containers
options.C: Puncture-proof sharps boxes
options.D: Yellow bags

explanation: General municipal-type waste that has no contact with infectious body fluids is discarded in black bins or bags. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: A nurse sustains a deep needle-stick injury from a patient known to be living with HIV. What is the immediate first-aid action the nurse should take?

options.A: Apply a tourniquet above the injury site to trap circulating pathogens
options.B: Cover the wound tightly with an adhesive bandage and continue the shift
options.C: Apply strong concentrated bleach directly into the wound puncture
options.D: Wash the puncture site immediately with soap and running water without aggressive squeezing

explanation: Washing with soap and water cleans the wound without damaging local tissues or driving pathogens deeper through milking or squeezing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: Within what maximum time window must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis for HIV ideally be initiated after a high-risk exposure?

options.A: Within 12 hours
options.B: Within 72 hours
options.C: Within 24 hours
options.D: Within 7 days

explanation: PEP is most effective when started immediately and must be initiated within 72 hours of exposure to prevent viral replication and seroconversion. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: How can a community health nurse best assist a family caring for a relative with a chronic draining wound at home?

options.A: Instruct them to burn all soiled dressings in an open backyard fire
options.B: Require the family to purchase hospital-grade biohazard bins for their kitchen
options.C: Advise them to stop changing dressings until a doctor visits the home
options.D: Provide education on hand hygiene, safe dressing disposal, and improvised barrier use

explanation: Community education equips home caregivers with practical skills to manage waste and maintain hygiene safely without complex clinical infrastructure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is a primary infection control challenge unique to home-based care compared to hospital environments?

options.A: Abundant supplies of industrial-grade disinfectants
options.B: Limited access to formal medical waste disposal infrastructure
options.C: Mandatory air filtration systems in every household
options.D: Constant supervision by occupational health physicians

explanation: Home care settings lack commercial incinerators and regulated waste disposal streams, requiring community nurses to teach safe alternative containment. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: To which patient population do standard precautions primarily apply?

options.A: Only patients diagnosed with active tuberculosis
options.B: All patients receiving healthcare services
options.C: Patients admitted to surgical wards exclusively
options.D: Individuals showing visible symptoms of bloodborne illness

explanation: Standard precautions are designed for universal application to every patient regardless of their infectious status to prevent pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary underlying assumption of standard precautions?

options.A: Infection risk is restricted strictly to patients with fevers
options.B: Healthy individuals cannot transmit hospital-acquired infections
options.C: Gloves eliminate the need for subsequent handwashing
options.D: All bodily fluids and moist tissues carry potential pathogens

explanation: This framework assumes that any patient's blood, body fluids, secretions, and non-intact skin can transmit infectious agents, justifying universal barrier use. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly preferred over alcohol-based rubs?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.B: After touching a patient's intact skin surface
options.C: Before entering a general medical ward
options.D: Immediately before applying sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Visible dirt and proteinaceous matter physically impede alcohol sanitizers, requiring mechanical removal through soap and water handwashing. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which moment is categorized as an indication for hand hygiene under standard guidelines?

options.A: Following the replacement of an unbroken IV fluid bag
options.B: Before documenting nursing notes at the central nurses station
options.C: Immediately after touching a patient's immediate environment
options.D: Directly after removing a clean, dry patient chart folder

explanation: Pathogens persist on bed rails and bedside tables, making hand hygiene mandatory after touching objects in the patient's immediate zone. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which piece of personal protective equipment is specifically required during aerosol-generating procedures for airborne pathogens?

options.A: Particulate respirator such as an N95
options.B: Disposable plastic face shield alone
options.C: Heavy-duty utility rubber gloves
options.D: Standard paper surgical face mask

explanation: Respirators filter out small airborne droplet nuclei generated during specific medical procedures, offering protection that standard surgical masks cannot match. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to irrigate a large, bleeding open wound. Which barrier combination is most appropriate?

options.A: Sterile gloves and standard surgical mask
options.B: Face mask and sterile surgical head covering
options.C: Gloves, waterproof gown, and face shield
options.D: Clean gloves and long-sleeved cloth lab coat

explanation: Wound irrigation generates splashes of blood and body fluids, requiring protection for hands, clothing, and facial mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the safest method for handling a contaminated needle if recapping is absolutely necessary?

options.A: Using both hands to securely guide the cap back on
options.B: Pressing the needle cap against a hard table surface
options.C: Employing a single-handed scoop technique
options.D: Holding the cap tightly with sterile surgical forceps

explanation: The one-handed scoop method keeps the non-dominant hand away from the sharp point, preventing accidental needlestick injuries during recapping. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to fill a sharps container past its designated fill line?

options.A: It interferes with the automatic sealing mechanism of the lid
options.B: It increases the risk of needlestick injuries for staff handling disposal
options.C: Overfilled containers cannot be incinerated in local facilities
options.D: The plastic container will chemically dissolve from excess weight

explanation: Protruding needles from overfilled bins expose nurses and housekeeping staff to sharp punctures during collection and transport. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: What immediate action should a person take when coughing or sneezing if a tissue is unavailable?

options.A: Cover the mouth tightly with both bare hands
options.B: Pinch the nostrils closed using the thumb and index finger
options.C: Direct the cough into the inner aspect of the elbow
options.D: Turn the head downward toward the open floor

explanation: Coughing into the upper sleeve or elbow prevents respiratory secretions from contaminating the hands, which frequently touch environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which intervention represents an effective environmental source control measure for respiratory pathogens?

options.A: Providing accessible tissues and alcohol-based rub at facility entrances
options.B: Restricting visitor access exclusively to pediatric inpatient units
options.C: Isheduling mandatory prophylactic antibiotic therapy for all visitors
options.D: Installing ultraviolet germicidal irradiation in hospital hallways

explanation: Placing supplies at entry points encourages immediate compliance with respiratory hygiene before individuals disperse through waiting areas. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which category of medical equipment requires high-level disinfection or sterilization before reuse?

options.A: Semi-critical items touching mucous membranes
options.B: Disposable linen hampers located in utility rooms
options.C: Non-critical items resting on intact patient skin
options.D: Environmental surfaces such as bedside tables

explanation: Semi-critical devices contact non-intact skin or mucous membranes and require rigorous high-level disinfection to eliminate microbial contamination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary rationale for cleaning environmental surfaces prior to applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Cleaning agents prevent the rapid evaporation of water from tiles
options.B: Organic soil can neutralize or inactivate many chemical disinfectants
options.C: Detergents provide a pleasant aroma that masks clinical odors
options.D: Pre-cleaning eliminates the need for any subsequent disinfection step

explanation: Dirt, blood, and protein films act as physical barriers that protect underlying microorganisms from direct contact with disinfectant solutions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: What immediate action is contraindicated following an accidental needlestick injury?

options.A: Reporting the incident immediately to a nursing supervisor
options.B: Washing the affected skin area with soap and water
options.C: Squeezing or aggressively scrubbing the puncture site
options.D: Flushing the surrounding skin thoroughly with running tap water

explanation: Squeezing or scrubbing traumatizes local tissues and can force pathogens deeper into the vascular bed, increasing transmission risk. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why is rapid reporting and evaluation crucial following an occupational blood exposure?

options.A: Source patients cannot be tested after twenty-four hours elapse
options.B: Administrative leave is mandatory for all exposed nursing staff
options.C: Hospital insurance policies require documentation within one hour
options.D: Post-exposure prophylaxis must be started quickly to maximize effectiveness

explanation: Prophylactic medications for viruses like HIV exhibit significantly higher success rates when administered within hours of exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)

question: What primary shift characterizes the epidemiological transition currently occurring in Nigeria?

options.A: A rapid decrease in overall population growth rates
options.B: A shift from urban to rural disease distribution
options.C: The complete eradication of vector-borne illnesses
options.D: The simultaneous burden of infectious and chronic diseases

explanation: Nigeria and many developing nations are experiencing a dual disease burden, managing both traditional infectious diseases and rising rates of non-communicable chronic conditions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a non-modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases?

options.A: High dietary sodium intake
options.B: Sedentary occupational habits
options.C: Regular tobacco smoking
options.D: Advanced chronological age

explanation: Age, genetic makeup, and family history are intrinsic biological factors that cannot be altered, unlike behavioral habits such as diet and exercise. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: How do modifiable risk factors primarily influence the development of chronic conditions?

options.A: They interact with biological vulnerabilities to accelerate cellular and vascular damage
options.B: They exclusively affect the lymphatic system within the first decade of life
options.C: They directly alter an individual's inherited genetic code over time
options.D: They prevent the body from absorbing essential micronutrients permanently

explanation: Lifestyle habits and environmental exposures compound over time, straining organ systems and promoting the pathological changes that manifest as chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of primary prevention strategies in healthcare?

options.A: To diagnose asymptomatic pathology using advanced laboratory tests
options.B: To rehabilitate patients following a major surgical intervention
options.C: To prevent the initial onset of disease in a healthy population
options.D: To halt the progression of an established clinical disease

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and health promotion before any pathological changes or disease states occur. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h3)

question: A community health nurse in a Nigerian market square wants to promote healthy nutrition. What is the most practical approach?

options.A: Promoting balanced meals using affordable, locally available foodstuffs
options.B: Instructing community members to fast for two days every week
options.C: Advocating for the exclusive consumption of raw, unprocessed grains
options.D: Distributing meal plans based exclusively on imported dietary supplements

explanation: Effective health promotion must be culturally appropriate and economically feasible, leveraging local agricultural produce that community members can easily access and afford. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h3)

question: What defines secondary prevention in the continuum of healthcare?

options.A: Enacting national legislation to ban harmful industrial pollutants
options.B: Providing palliative comfort measures for terminal illnesses
options.C: Screening for early, asymptomatic disease to allow prompt treatment
options.D: Restoring physical mobility following a disabling stroke

explanation: Secondary prevention targets individuals with early or subclinical disease through screening tests to catch conditions before they cause severe damage. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main advantage of implementing opportunistic screening in busy Nigerian primary healthcare clinics?

options.A: It guarantees 100 percent compliance with prescribed dietary regimens
options.B: It captures individuals who would otherwise not attend routine wellness visits
options.C: It completely replaces the necessity for long-term pharmacological treatment
options.D: It eliminates the need for any diagnostic equipment whatsoever

explanation: Since routine preventive health checks are uncommon, screening patients who present for acute ailments maximizes the opportunity to detect hidden chronic conditions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which factor represents a major barrier to chronic medication adherence in many Nigerian clinical settings?

options.A: Excessive availability of free pharmaceutical supplies
options.B: Overly simplistic dosing schedules prescribed by physicians
options.C: Too few chronic conditions existing within the population
options.D: Out-of-pocket costs and fake or substandard drugs

explanation: Financial constraints combined with the risk of purchasing counterfeit medications severely undermine consistent long-term drug therapy for chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why must the management of non-communicable diseases differ from acute care approaches?

options.A: Chronic diseases never require laboratory monitoring or diagnostic testing
options.B: Acute care is exclusively practiced in rural community health posts
options.C: Chronic diseases always resolve spontaneously without medical intervention
options.D: Acute care focuses on permanent cures, whereas chronic care requires lifelong management

explanation: Unlike a short-term infection that resolves with a course of antibiotics, chronic conditions persist indefinitely and require sustained lifestyle and pharmacological management. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the community health nurse in NCD control?

options.A: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for national distribution
options.B: Performing complex open-heart surgeries in primary clinics
options.C: Conducting community outreach, screening, and health education
options.D: Enforcing strict punitive fines for unhealthy dietary habits

explanation: Community health nurses focus on health promotion, early detection through screening, and educating populations directly within their local environments. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is establishing patient support groups valuable for individuals managing chronic illnesses?

options.A: They replace the professional nursing assessment process entirely
options.B: They supply free imported medications to all participating members
options.C: They provide emotional encouragement and foster shared coping strategies
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for ongoing medical check-ups

explanation: Support groups build social capital and psychological resilience, helping patients navigate the challenges of living with a lifelong condition. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following interventions is an example of a fiscal policy used to control non-communicable diseases?

options.A: Mandating hospital admission for individuals with high cholesterol
options.B: Placing high taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages and tobacco
options.C: Banning the construction of all commercial food markets
options.D: Providing free gym memberships for every citizen over age sixty

explanation: Taxation policies make unhealthy products less affordable, effectively reducing consumption at the population level. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is multisectoral collaboration essential for effective non-communicable disease control?

options.A: International donors will not fund health programs managed by nurses
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to collaborate with nurses on chronic disease management
options.C: Infectious diseases can only be controlled by agricultural ministries
options.D: Health ministries alone cannot influence the underlying social and environmental determinants of health

explanation: The root causes of NCDs—such as diet, physical environment, and commercial product marketing—are governed by sectors outside of traditional healthcare, necessitating a whole-of-government approach. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary anatomical location where cervical cancer typically originates?

options.A: The fallopian tube fimbriae
options.B: The fundus of the uterus
options.C: The ovarian cortex
options.D: The transformation zone

explanation: Cervical cancer primarily develops in the transformation zone, where the endocervical and ectocervical cell types meet and undergo active cellular turnover. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is cervical cancer considered a significant public health concern in Nigeria?

options.A: Rapid metastatic spread prior to primary infection
options.B: Strict federal bans on prophylactic vaccines
options.C: Limited access to routine screening infrastructure
options.D: High rates of spontaneous genetic mutations in the population

explanation: Resource-constrained settings often lack widespread, accessible screening programs, leading to delayed diagnoses at advanced stages of the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which specific viral strains are most commonly responsible for high-risk cervical cancer development?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus type 1
options.B: HPV types 6 and 11
options.C: Herpes Simplex Virus type 2
options.D: HPV types 16 and 18

explanation: High-risk strains HPV 16 and 18 account for the majority of invasive cervical carcinomas worldwide. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: How does HIV co-infection directly impact the natural history of HPV in the cervix?

options.A: It neutralizes the inflammatory response required for tumor growth
options.B: It impairs immune-mediated viral clearance, promoting persistence
options.C: It accelerates the immediate shedding of healthy squamous cells
options.D: It converts high-risk viral strains into benign epithelial warts

explanation: Compromised cell-mediated immunity in HIV-positive individuals prevents the body from clearing viral loads, drastically raising the risk of persistent infection. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the HPV E6 oncoprotein within infected host cells?

options.A: Enhances basement membrane stability against invasion
options.B: Stimulates the direct production of protective antibodies
options.C: Inactivates the retinoblastoma protein to halt mitosis
options.D: Promotes the degradation of the p53 tumor suppressor protein

explanation: The E6 oncoprotein targets p53 for destruction, preventing damaged cells from undergoing programmed cell death and allowing mutations to accumulate. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: What pathological finding defines the progression from cervical intraepithelial neoplasia to invasive cancer?

options.A: Inflammatory necrosis of the ectocervical surface
options.B: Breaching of the epithelial basement membrane
options.C: Complete clearance of the viral genome from basal cells
options.D: Transformation of squamous cells into glandular tissue

explanation: Invasive cancer occurs only when abnormal cells break through the basement membrane and invade the underlying stromal tissues. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the most characteristic early symptom of cervical cancer?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Foul-smelling purulent stool
options.C: Acute upper abdominal pain
options.D: Severe bilateral lower limb edema

explanation: Post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding is typically the first physical warning sign prompting clinical evaluation for cervical pathology. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer presents with unilateral leg swelling and back pain. What pathophysiological mechanism best explains this finding?

options.A: Metastatic bone lesions settling exclusively in the femur
options.B: Acute inflammatory reaction following routine biopsy
options.C: Systemic cachexia leading to generalized third-spacing
options.D: Tumor compression of pelvic wall structures and nerve plexuses

explanation: Advanced pelvic tumor extension can obstruct venous and lymphatic drainage causing leg edema, while nerve compression leads to referred back and pelvic pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: What visual change occurs when acetic acid is applied to abnormal cervical tissue during a VIA screening?

options.A: The tissue turns an acetowhite color
options.B: The lesion develops bright yellow ulcerations
options.C: The mucosa undergoes rapid hyperpigmentation
options.D: The affected area produces active bleeding

explanation: Abnormal cellular changes have higher nuclear protein concentrations that coagulate and reflect light as a distinct acetowhite patch upon acid application. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: A community health nurse in a rural clinic uses a screen-and-treat protocol with VIA. What is the primary advantage of this operational approach?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any physical examination of the cervix
options.B: It provides definitive histological confirmation of invasive carcinoma
options.C: It completely replaces the need for HPV vaccination in young girls
options.D: It minimizes loss to follow-up by providing same-day treatment for positive results

explanation: In rural settings, patients often fail to return for delayed lab results; treating immediately upon a positive visual inspection drastically improves clinical compliance. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a colposcopy after an abnormal Pap smear?

options.A: To magnify and closely inspect the cervix for biopsy targeting
options.B: To destroy all superficial pathogens causing vaginal discharge
options.C: To administer localized radiation therapy to the tumor bed
options.D: To measure systemic hormone levels driving cell growth

explanation: Colposcopy uses magnification and staining agents to locate abnormal vascular and epithelial patterns so the clinician can take targeted punch biopsies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why is Lugol's iodine solution applied to the cervix during diagnostic evaluations?

options.A: It acts as a potent local anesthetic to numb the cervical stroma before biopsy
options.B: It permanently sterilizes the transformation zone against recurring viral loads
options.C: Healthy glycogen-rich cells take up the brown stain, while abnormal cells remain unstained
options.D: It stimulates immediate regression of high-grade intraepithelial lesions

explanation: Normal mature squamous cells contain abundant glycogen which stains brown with iodine, whereas dysplastic or malignant cells lack glycogen and appear pale or yellow (Schiller-positive). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the standard primary treatment approach for locally advanced cervical cancer?

options.A: Total abdominal colectomy
options.B: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy
options.C: Radical trachelectomy alone
options.D: Cryotherapy and observation

explanation: Locally advanced lesions respond best to a combined regimen of external/internal radiation alongside sensitizing chemotherapy rather than surgery alone. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: What role does cisplatin typically serve when administered alongside radiotherapy in cervical cancer management?

options.A: It completely prevents local tissue fibrosis caused by radiation beams
options.B: It suppresses systemic bone marrow activity to stop white blood cell growth
options.C: It replaces the need for surgical removal of pelvic lymph nodes
options.D: It acts as a radiosensitizer to make cancer cells more vulnerable to radiation

explanation: Cisplatin is administered concurrently in low doses to sensitize tumor cells to the cytotoxic effects of ionizing radiation, improving local control rates. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: A patient undergoing pelvic radiation therapy for cervical cancer reports burning urination and frequent urgency. What nursing assessment is most appropriate?

options.A: Advise the patient to completely stop drinking all fluids to rest the bladder
options.B: Prepare the patient immediately for emergency surgical closure of a fistula
options.C: Monitor for signs of radiation-induced cystitis and urinary tract irritation
options.D: Check for signs of acute metastatic spread to the cerebral cortex

explanation: Radiation to pelvic fields commonly irritates the bladder mucosa, resulting in inflammatory symptoms resembling a urinary tract infection known as radiation cystitis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: What is a primary focus when delivering palliative nursing care to a patient with terminal cervical cancer?

options.A: Focusing solely on routine preventative screening for secondary malignancies
options.B: Enforcing strict bedrest with complete isolation from family members
options.C: Optimizing comfort, pain management, and holistic family support
options.D: Aggressively titrating high-dose chemotherapeutic agents to achieve remission

explanation: Palliative nursing shifts the goal from curative treatment to symptom control, pain relief, and emotional support to ensure quality of life at the end of life. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h8)

question: At what age group are prophylactic HPV vaccination programs primarily targeted for maximum clinical effectiveness?

options.A: Infants immediately following routine neonatal immunizations
options.B: Adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years before sexual debut
options.C: Adult women over the age of 50 during routine menopause clinics
options.D: Pregnant women during their second trimester antenatal visits

explanation: Vaccines generate the highest antibody response and protect best when given prior to any potential exposure to the human papillomavirus through sexual contact. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: Why is the combination of HPV vaccination and routine screening considered the ultimate dual-layered defense against cervical cancer?

options.A: Screening eliminates the need for any follow-up care if the vaccine was administered
options.B: Vaccination prevents new infections, while screening catches pre-existing or breakthrough lesions early
options.C: Vaccination neutralizes all known non-viral forms of gynecological malignancies
options.D: Vaccination cures active invasive tumors, while screening repairs damaged vaginal tissue

explanation: Prophylactic vaccines stop future infections from targeted strains, but screening remains necessary to catch abnormalities caused by non-vaccine strains or pre-existing infections. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: What is the approximate percentage of lung cancer cases classified as Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

options.A: Eighty-five percent
options.B: Fifteen percent
options.C: Ninety-nine percent
options.D: Fifty percent

explanation: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer is the predominant form, making up about 85% of all diagnosed lung malignancies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is Small Cell Lung Cancer considered clinically distinct from Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

options.A: It responds exclusively to surgical resection alone
options.B: It originates entirely from the pleura rather than bronchi
options.C: It displays an aggressive growth pattern with early metastasis
options.D: It occurs exclusively in patients who have never smoked

explanation: Small Cell Lung Cancer is characterized by rapid cellular division and an aggressive tendency to spread to distant sites early in the disease course. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is identified as the leading cause of lung cancer among individuals who have never smoked?

options.A: Bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Dietary deficiencies
options.D: Radon gas exposure

explanation: Natural radioactive radon gas accumulating indoors is the primary risk factor for non-smokers who develop lung cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: How do occupational hazards like asbestos interact with tobacco smoke to influence cancer risk?

options.A: They exclusively cause benign rather than malignant tumors
options.B: They neutralize the toxic effects of tobacco tars
options.C: They delay the onset of symptoms by twenty years
options.D: They multiply the overall carcinogenic risk exponentially

explanation: Exposure to workplace carcinogens like asbestos combined with cigarette smoking creates a multiplicative, rather than merely additive, risk for malignant transformation. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which genetic alteration is frequently involved in the development of lung malignancies?

options.A: Inactivation of tumor suppressor genes
options.B: Enhancement of surfactant production
options.C: Duplication of normal hemoglobin genes
options.D: Suppression of cellular division pathways

explanation: Mutations that deactivate protective tumor suppressor genes, such as p53, allow damaged cells to replicate uncontrollably. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: A patient with advanced lung cancer develops sudden confusion and severe headaches. Which pathophysiological process best accounts for these new symptoms?

options.A: Accumulation of pleural fluid in the thorax
options.B: Metastatic spread of cancer cells to the brain
options.C: Direct compression of the superior vena cava
options.D: Development of primary obstructive pneumonia

explanation: The brain is a common site for hematogenous metastasis from lung tumors, leading to neurological changes such as headaches and confusion. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is a frequent early local symptom of an enlarging pulmonary tumor?

options.A: Severe generalized peripheral edema
options.B: Painful ulceration of the skin
options.C: A persistent, worsening cough
options.D: Sudden loss of visual acuity

explanation: Irritation of the bronchial mucosa by a growing mass commonly triggers a new or changing cough that does not resolve with standard treatments. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why does hemoptysis frequently occur in individuals with advanced bronchial malignancies?

options.A: Excessive mucus production ruptures the major airways
options.B: Tumor erosion into pulmonary blood vessels leads to bleeding
options.C: Chemotherapy agents directly damage the pleural lining
options.D: Systemic hypertension bursts fragile alveolar walls

explanation: As the malignant neoplasm invades surrounding tissues, it erodes mucosal blood vessels, causing blood-tinged sputum or frank hemoptysis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is required to establish a definitive diagnosis of lung cancer?

options.A: Performing a bedside spirometry test
options.B: Exclusively viewing a routine chest radiograph
options.C: Measuring baseline serum electrolyte levels
options.D: Histological tissue confirmation via biopsy

explanation: Imaging alone suggests malignancy, but a definitive diagnosis requires examining tissue samples obtained through biopsy or bronchoscopy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of utilizing the TNM staging system in pulmonary malignancy?

options.A: To calculate the exact concentration of environmental carcinogens
options.B: To predict the patient's exact occupational history
options.C: To evaluate tumor size, lymph node involvement, and distant spread
options.D: To measure the patient's daily physical activity tolerance

explanation: The TNM system standardizes the classification of cancer by assessing the primary tumor, regional lymph nodes, and presence of metastasis to direct treatment options. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which treatment modality is typically the primary therapeutic choice for localized Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: High-dose oxygen therapy
options.C: Therapeutic thoracentesis
options.D: Surgical resection

explanation: When caught early and localized, removing the tumor surgically provides the highest potential for cure in non-small cell cases. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is surgery rarely used as the sole treatment for Small Cell Lung Cancer?

options.A: The cancer has usually metastasized microscopically by the time of diagnosis
options.B: Patients with small cell lung cancer never have sufficient lung capacity
options.C: Radiation therapy destroys the tumor before surgery can be scheduled
options.D: Small cell tumors are completely resistant to all forms of surgical cutting

explanation: Because small cell lung cancer is exceptionally aggressive and spreads early, systemic therapy like chemotherapy and radiation are prioritized over isolated surgery. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is a primary focus of nursing interventions for a patient receiving medical treatment for lung cancer?

options.A: Optimizing respiratory function and managing side effects
options.B: Prescribing appropriate chemotherapeutic regimens
options.C: Determining the exact TNM surgical stage
options.D: Performing routine diagnostic CT scans independently

explanation: Nurses play a central role in monitoring breathing, maintaining oxygenation, and alleviating the physical and emotional side effects of therapy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy for lung cancer reports severe, debilitating fatigue. Which nursing approach is most appropriate to include in the care plan?

options.A: Recommending high-intensity daily aerobic exercise routines
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to decrease metabolic energy expenditure
options.C: Encouraging a balance between periods of physical activity and rest
options.D: Insisting on complete bed rest until chemotherapy treatments finish

explanation: Balancing rest with light, tolerable activity helps manage cancer-related fatigue without leading to the deconditioning caused by total bed rest. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: What represents the most effective primary prevention strategy against lung cancer?

options.A: Tobacco use prevention and smoking cessation
options.B: Mandatory annual chest radiography for all citizens
options.C: Widespread administration of targeted vaccines
options.D: Prophylactic surgical removal of bronchial tissue

explanation: Preventing tobacco initiation and helping current smokers quit addresses the leading cause of lung malignancies globally. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h8)

question: Which screening tool is recommended for early detection of lung cancer in high-risk individuals?

options.A: Low-dose computed tomography scan
options.B: Routine diagnostic sputum cytology
options.C: Pulmonary function spirometry testing
options.D: Standard resting electrocardiogram

explanation: Low-dose CT screening has been proven effective in detecting early-stage lung tumors in high-risk patients, improving survival outcomes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h8)

question: What primary characteristic defines an accident in a public health context?

options.A: It is a chronic condition with a slow, insidious onset
options.B: It is a genetically predetermined physiological failure
options.C: It is a pathogen-driven systemic inflammatory response
options.D: It is an unexpected event resulting in injury or damage

explanation: Accidents are classified as sudden, unplanned incidents that cause physical harm or property loss rather than slow-developing chronic diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: How do community health nurses typically view the occurrence of accidents?

options.A: As biological phenomena resulting from subclinical infections
options.B: As unavoidable tragedies dictated entirely by random chance
options.C: As predictable events linked to specific environmental and behavioral factors
options.D: As direct consequences of inherited metabolic disorders

explanation: Modern health frameworks treat accidents as preventable occurrences driven by identifiable risk factors rather than unpreventable acts of fate. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is a frequent cause of accidental poisoning among young children in many Nigerian households?

options.A: Storing kerosene inside empty beverage bottles
options.B: Consuming over-the-counter multivitamin syrups
options.C: Inhaling fumes from indoor charcoal heating
options.D: Eating unwashed vegetables from local markets

explanation: Young children easily mistake brightly colored kerosene stored in soft drink bottles for potable liquids, leading to accidental ingestion and severe chemical pneumonitis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which setting accounts for a high proportion of trauma cases managed in Nigerian emergency departments?

options.A: Road transport corridors and crowded domestic environments
options.B: Deep-sea commercial fishing vessels offshore
options.C: High-altitude mountaineering recreational camps
options.D: Controlled sterile laboratory environments

explanation: Road traffic crashes and household mishaps represent the vast majority of acute trauma seen in local healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following represents an environmental risk factor for domestic accidents?

options.A: Driver fatigue after a long overnight journey
options.B: Failure to service a commercial vehicle's brakes
options.C: Consuming alcohol before operating machinery
options.D: Cluttered walkways and poor lighting in the home

explanation: Environmental factors refer to physical conditions in the surroundings, such as obstacles and poor illumination, that facilitate slips, trips, and falls. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h3)

question: What makes developmental age a significant human risk factor for accidental injuries?

options.A: Limited hazard awareness and immature motor coordination in children
options.B: Decreased bone density occurring exclusively during adolescence
options.C: Complete absence of sensory perception during middle age
options.D: Heightened physical stamina and rapid reflex actions in adults

explanation: Children lack the cognitive maturity to recognize danger and possess developing motor skills, making them highly susceptible to accidental harm. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is a common psychological consequence experienced by survivors of severe accidents?

options.A: Seasonal affective disorder
options.B: Bipolar mood disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Obsessive compulsive disorder

explanation: The sudden and life-threatening nature of major accidents frequently triggers psychological trauma, manifesting as post-traumatic stress disorder in survivors. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h4)

question: How do widespread road traffic accidents impact the broader healthcare system?

options.A: They primarily increase funding available for elective surgical procedures
options.B: They reduce overall hospital admissions by promoting community health
options.C: They strain emergency services and deplete resources needed for other care
options.D: They eliminate the need for specialized surgical units in rural clinics

explanation: A high volume of emergency trauma cases consumes substantial blood supplies, medications, and personnel time, limiting capacity for other health services. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Golden Hour' in emergency trauma care?

options.A: To initiate life-saving interventions within sixty minutes of injury
options.B: To wait for specialized physicians to arrive before touching the patient
options.C: To allow the patient time to recover consciousness spontaneously
options.D: To complete administrative documentation prior to medical treatment

explanation: The golden hour refers to the critical window where prompt medical and surgical care significantly reduces mortality and permanent disability. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h5)

question: During the primary survey of an accident victim, what action should be prioritized immediately after ensuring airway patency?

options.A: Documenting the exact financial status of the patient
options.B: Evaluating breathing and checking for adequate chest movement
options.C: Obtaining a detailed past medical history from family members
options.D: Cleaning minor abrasions with an antiseptic solution

explanation: Following the ABCDE protocol, airway management is followed directly by assessing and supporting breathing before moving to circulation and secondary concerns. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which complication of immobility should nurses actively prevent in recovering accident patients confined to bed?

options.A: Enhanced respiratory capacity and elevated blood pressure
options.B: Hyperactive delirium and excessive weight loss
options.C: Rapid bone mineralization and increased muscle tone
options.D: Pressure ulcers and deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Prolonged bed rest impairs circulation and puts pressure on bony prominences, making pressure sores and blood clots major risks for immobile patients. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team approach essential during the rehabilitation phase of injury recovery?

options.A: It replaces the need for pharmacological pain management interventions
options.B: It addresses the complex physical, psychological, and social needs of the patient
options.C: It ensures that nurses are completely absolved of all direct care duties
options.D: It guarantees that hospital discharge occurs within twenty-four hours

explanation: Recovery from severe trauma requires coordinated expertise from nursing, physiotherapy, social work, and medicine to achieve optimal functional outcomes. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is considered the most cost-effective strategy for reducing trauma burdens in a population?

options.A: Increasing the availability of emergency blood transfusions
options.B: Expanding intensive care unit bed capacities in cities
options.C: Accident prevention and community safety education
options.D: Importing advanced surgical robotics for trauma centers

explanation: Preventative measures stop injuries from occurring in the first place, saving lives and resources far more efficiently than treating severe trauma. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which activity best illustrates the role of a community health nurse in accident prevention?

options.A: Investigating the financial auditing records of transport companies
options.B: Prescribing analgesic medications for chronic post-injury pain
options.C: Performing emergency orthopedic surgeries in a district hospital
options.D: Conducting workshops on home hazard identification and safe storage

explanation: Community health nurses focus on proactive education and hazard awareness to empower families to eliminate risks before injuries happen. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h7)

question: What defines a poison in the context of community health and toxicology?

options.A: A chemical compound that only affects the respiratory tract
options.B: Biological agents that cause chronic degenerative illnesses
options.C: An exclusively synthetic drug taken in supratherapeutic doses
options.D: Any substance that alters physiological functions harmfully

explanation: A poison is broadly defined as any agent that causes detrimental physiological changes regardless of whether it is natural, synthetic, solid, liquid, or gas. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why are agricultural seasons particularly hazardous regarding domestic poisoning in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Extreme weather changes cause household chemicals to spontaneously combust
options.B: Pesticides and herbicides are often stored in unlabelled containers near living areas
options.C: Local water treatment plants fail to filter out heavy metals during rains
options.D: Rural residents consume wild toxic plants due to seasonal food scarcity

explanation: During farming seasons, agricultural chemicals like organophosphates are frequently brought close to homes and stored improperly, increasing accidental ingestion risks. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which household item is most commonly implicated in accidental chemical pneumonitis among toddlers in West Africa?

options.A: Kerosene
options.B: Table salt
options.C: Paracetamol
options.D: Bleach

explanation: Kerosene is frequently stored in accessible bottles around homes and aspiration during ingestion causes severe chemical pneumonitis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h2)
